summary: Biltmore Records was a United States record label active from 1949 through 1951, headquartered in New York City. The label mainly issued reissues of recordings that were no longer in other labels' catalogues. RCA Victor sued Biltmore after discovering unauthorized reissues of material Victor had originally recorded, which ended the label's business.
one_line: Biltmore Records was a New York City-based US record label (1949-1951) known for reissues, shut down after an RCA Victor lawsuit.
key_facts: Biltmore Records was a United States based record label.
Biltmore Records was active from 1949 through 1951.
The label was headquartered in New York City.
Biltmore Records were often reissues of recordings no longer in the catalogues of other labels.
RCA Victor found out that Biltmore were making unauthorized reissues of material originally recorded by Victor.
RCA Victor sued Biltmore over the unauthorized reissues.
The lawsuit by RCA Victor put Biltmore out of business.
